home.seoTitle: PseudoLearn 2.0 · Learn to think like a programmer
home.seoDescription: A complete programming language in Spanish or English and a free app for macOS, Windows, iPhone and iPad: {lessons} lessons and {exercises} exercises that teach problem solving, with step-by-step execution and an optional AI assistant.
home.hero.title: Learn to think like a programmer.
home.hero.lead: PseudoLearn is a complete programming language you write in Spanish or English, and an app that teaches you to solve problems with it. Every step of your program is visible; every error is explained.
home.hero.requirements: Free · macOS · Windows · iPhone and iPad · Works offline · VS Code and terminal, coming soon
home.preview.alt: PseudoLearn with the Guided Demo program already run: the source code, its flowchart and the lines the program wrote.
download.mobileInput: Key bar with the language keywords
download.windowsInstallation: For your user only, no administrator rights
download.upcomingText: Linux and Android. No announced date: they will be published here when they are ready, not before.
download.windowsGuide.lead: From the Microsoft Store the app installs without warnings. The direct installer is not digitally signed yet, so Microsoft Defender SmartScreen stops it the first time.
download.windowsGuide.stepBrowser: If your browser says the file is not commonly downloaded, choose Keep. In Edge it sits in the warning’s … menu, followed by Show more and Keep anyway.
download.windowsGuide.stepMoreInfo: Open PseudoLearn-Setup.exe. When the blue screen appears, click More info, below the warning text.
download.windowsGuide.stepRunAnyway: Check that the app is PseudoLearn-Setup.exe and click Run anyway.
download.windowsGuide.stepInstall: Follow the installer. It does not ask for administrator rights, and the installed app opens without repeating the warning.
download.windowsGuide.note: Only download the installer from this page. If it reaches you any other way, do not run it. Once the installer is signed, these steps will no longer be needed.
home.closing.title: Start from zero: {lessons} lessons in {duration}.
home.closing.lead: By the end you will have solved real problems, written your first programs and learned to test them. From there, the rest of the path makes sense.

contact.seoDescription: Write to report a bug, propose a feature, suggest an improvement or settle a question about PseudoLearn. The same person who writes the code reads it.
contact.hero.title: Tell me what is missing, what is broken or what does not make sense.
contact.hero.lead: There is no suggestion box here that nobody opens. The same person who writes the code reads it, and a feature you miss weighs as much as a bug. It may take a few days to reply, but it replies.
contact.form.title: What do you want to tell me about?
contact.form.note: Pick one and the questions adjust. Fields marked with an asterisk are required.
contact.reason.error.title: Something is broken
contact.reason.error.description: A bug, an odd result, something that crashes.
contact.reason.feature.title: Something is missing
contact.reason.feature.description: A feature you need that is not there.
contact.reason.improvement.title: It could be better
contact.reason.question.title: I have a question
contact.reason.question.description: About the language, a module or the app.
contact.branch.error.label: So it can be reproduced

contact.branch.error.snippetHelp: Plain text, up to 4000 characters. No attachments needed.
contact.branch.feature.label: Before the idea, the problem
contact.branch.feature.intro: If you tell me the feature you want, I build that feature. If you tell me what you wanted it for, sometimes there is a better solution neither of us had thought of.

contact.branch.improvement.label: Where the friction is

contact.branch.improvement.frictionLabel: What took more effort than it should?
contact.branch.improvement.frictionPlace: Finding the object column among so many
contact.branch.question.label: About what
contact.branch.question.subjectLabel: Lesson or part of the specification
contact.branch.question.generalOption: Another question about the language or the app
contact.branch.question.subjectHelp: The lessons of the path, grouped by part, and the parts of the specification.
contact.branch.question.notice: The path and the specification are also inside the app, offline. Check them first in case they save you the wait.

privacy.seoDescription: How we handle your data in PseudoLearn: fully functional without an account, local storage, and zero analytics or advertising.
privacy.hero.title: Your code stays on your device.
privacy.hero.lead: PseudoLearn works completely without an account. If you do not sign in, your algorithms and progress never leave your machine: no server ever receives them.
privacy.summary.title: Executive summary
privacy.summary.lead: Our privacy policy rests upon three core principles that guide the design of the application:
privacy.summary.pillar1Text: The app is 100% functional without signing in. Neither your code nor your progress leaves your computer, unless you use Nodo, the optional AI assistant, and only after you give it your consent.
privacy.summary.pillar2Text: Your algorithms are saved as plain .pseudo text files on your own disk.
privacy.summary.pillar3Text: No behavioral telemetry, no advertising, no data sales, and no training AI models with your code.
privacy.toc.title: On this page
privacy.nav.supportText: If you have any questions regarding your data or wish to exercise your rights, write to us directly:
privacy.section.data.title: Data we process
privacy.section.data.lead: The volume of information we process depends strictly on how you choose to use PseudoLearn.
privacy.section.data.cardNoAccountTitle: If you use the app without an account: none
privacy.section.data.cardNoAccountText: The algorithms you write, your progress through the knowledge base, and your preferences are kept solely within the app directory on your device. We have no access to them and no technical means of recovering them.
privacy.section.data.cardAccountTitle: If you choose to sign in (optional)
privacy.section.data.cardAccountText: An account only enables backup and synchronization across your devices. It stores your user identifier, email address, display name or photo if provided by your login provider, algorithm metadata and contents, completed modules, and general preferences.
privacy.section.data.cardContactTitle: If you contact us via the web form
privacy.section.data.cardContactText: We process your contact reason, email, message, and any program snippet you voluntarily paste. Your browser environment telemetry is only transmitted if you check the corresponding box, and your IP address is sent to the anti-bot service solely to verify you are human.
privacy.section.data.calloutTitle: What we do not do by product decision
privacy.section.data.calloutText: We do not implement usage analytics, behavioral telemetry, advertising, or user profiling. We do not track how long it takes you to solve an exercise or rank you against other learners. We never sell data to third parties, and we never use your code to train artificial intelligence models.
privacy.section.storage.title: Where data is stored
privacy.section.storage.lead: Your data resides primarily on your local machine and, secondarily and encrypted, in European infrastructure.
privacy.section.storage.deviceText: Your programs are always saved as plain-text .pseudo files alongside a local index. That is the primary, self-contained copy, whether you have an account or not.
privacy.section.storage.cloudText: Only if you chose to sign in. Supabase is our authentication and database provider. All data travels encrypted over HTTPS/TLS, and the backend enforces Row-Level Security (RLS) so each account can only access its own records. Session tokens are stored securely in your system Keychain.
privacy.section.storage.webText: The website runs on Cloudflare Workers and does not retain databases of form submissions. The contact form generates a secure email dispatched through Oracle Cloud (Frankfurt) directly to our support inbox.
privacy.section.storage.assetsText: The website does not request fonts or scripts from third-party hosts to ensure your IP address is not shared. Only your theme and language choices are stored locally, which is why you will never see cookie consent banners or trackers.
privacy.section.auth.title: Account access and age requirements
privacy.section.auth.lead: Authentication is handled through established identity providers or direct magic links.
privacy.section.auth.providersText: You can sign in with Apple, Google, or a magic link sent to your email. If you use Sign in with Apple and conceal your address, we receive Apple private relay address and never your real inbox.
privacy.section.auth.ageText: Creating an account requires being at least 16 years of age or the legal minimum in your country with parental consent. However, the app can be used without an account at any age with complete safety.
privacy.section.deletion.title: Deleting your account and data
privacy.section.deletion.lead: We guarantee the right to permanent deletion directly and without bureaucratic hurdles.
privacy.section.deletion.selfServiceText: You can delete your account at any time via Settings → Account → Delete account. Upon confirmation, your cloud account, synced algorithms, learning progress, and cloud preferences are permanently and immediately purged.
privacy.section.deletion.localRetentionT: Deleting your account does not remove algorithms saved locally on your machine to prevent accidental data loss. When signing out, you can choose whether to keep or remove local files.
privacy.section.deletion.manualText: You may also request account deletion by emailing support@pseudolearn.com from your registered address. Requests are processed within 30 days, with backup snapshots rotating within a maximum 30-day window.
privacy.section.retention.title: Retention periods
privacy.section.retention.lead: We adhere to strict data minimization and finite retention periods.
privacy.section.retention.itemDevice: Local files on your device: kept until you delete them or uninstall the application.
privacy.section.retention.itemSync: Synchronized records: for the lifetime of your active account. Deleted algorithms retain a 90-day technical tombstone marker solely to propagate deletion to other devices.
privacy.section.retention.itemSupport: Support communications: kept for 24 months from the last reply to ensure continuity in issue resolution.
privacy.section.retention.itemInactivity: Inactive accounts: if an account remains unused for 24 months, an email notification will precede its automatic deletion.
privacy.section.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.section.rights.lead: We uphold rigorous international standards for personal data protection.
privacy.section.rights.text1: You have the right to access, rectify, cancel, and oppose the processing of your personal data (ARCO rights under Peru Law No. 29733, as well as rights of erasure, restriction, and data portability under the GDPR in the EU and the CCPA in California).
privacy.section.rights.text2: Your files belong to you: you can export all your algorithms in plain text at any time directly from the app. For additional requests, email us at support@pseudolearn.com (response within 30 days).
privacy.section.rights.text3: We do not sell or share personal information with commercial advertisers, meaning no opt-out configuration is ever required.
privacy.section.contact.title: Changes and contact
privacy.section.contact.lead: We maintain full transparency with our community regarding policy updates.
privacy.section.contact.text1: Any future updates to this policy will appear on this page along with an updated effective date. If a change is material and you hold an active account, we will notify you by email.
privacy.section.contact.text2: For any inquiries regarding your privacy, contact us at support@pseudolearn.com. You will receive a direct, personal response from the creator of the project.

home.nodo.title: A companion that guides you without solving it for you.
home.nodo.lead: Nodo is PseudoLearn’s AI assistant: it knows the app and the language, sees the screen you are on and checks every program with the engine before suggesting it. It is optional, with a monthly subscription and a {days}-day free trial.
nodo.name: Nodo
nodo.chat.label: Sample conversation with Nodo
nodo.chat.question: Why does my program say 2 buses are enough for 95 students?
nodo.chat.answer: Your program uses div, which keeps only the whole part: 95 div 40 is 2, and the 15 students left over get no bus.
nodo.chat.followUp: Try it by hand: do 95 students fit in 2 buses of 40? Which function rounds up?
nodo.chat.confirm: Nodo wants to create an algorithm with your fix.
nodo.chat.disclaimer: Nodo is an AI and can make mistakes.
nodo.seoDescription: Nodo is PseudoLearn’s AI assistant: it explains errors, checks every program with the engine and guides you through exercises without giving away the answer. Monthly subscription with a 7-day free trial.
nodo.hero.title: An assistant that teaches you to think, not to copy.
nodo.hero.lead: Nodo knows PseudoLearn, sees the screen you are on and checks every program with the engine before showing it to you. It explains, gives hints and walks you through exercises without giving you the answer.
nodo.hero.cta: Get the app and try it free for {days} days
nodo.hero.note: In the app, tap the Nodo button on any screen or go to Settings → Nodo.
nodo.what.title: What Nodo does.
nodo.what.lead: Nodo works on what is in front of you: the open algorithm, the lesson you are reading or the exercise you are trying.
nodo.what.explain.title: Explains a diagnostic
nodo.what.explain.text: It tells you what the error means, where it starts and which section of the specification covers it.
nodo.what.check.title: Checks before suggesting
nodo.what.check.text: Every code block it writes goes through the PseudoLearn engine and arrives marked “Verified” or “With errors”.
nodo.what.guide.title: Guides without solving for you
nodo.what.guide.text: In an exercise it gives graded hints. The solution only appears if you ask for it and confirm.
nodo.what.work.title: Works with you in the app
nodo.what.work.text: It creates and edits algorithms, changes arguments, opens lessons or builds your own exercises, always with your permission.
nodo.rules.title: Rules Nodo never breaks.
nodo.rules.lead: An assistant for students has to be predictable. These rules are built into the app, not a promise.
nodo.rules.parity.title: Nothing you could not do
nodo.rules.parity.text: Nodo has no hidden features: each of its actions uses the same operation as the button you would tap.
nodo.rules.confirm.title: Asks for permission
nodo.rules.confirm.text: Before creating, editing or deleting it shows what it wants to do, and warns you when something cannot be undone.
nodo.rules.verify.title: Checked code
nodo.rules.verify.text: It does not hand you a program without analyzing it and, when needed, running it with the engine.
nodo.rules.honest.title: Always clearly an AI
nodo.rules.honest.text: It shows as “Nodo · AI” and reminds you it can make mistakes. The last word belongs to you and the engine.
nodo.plans.title: Nodo plans.
nodo.plans.lead: The app is free and complete. Nodo is optional and runs on credits: each question spends what it takes to answer it, and the app shows your balance and the cost of the last one.
nodo.plans.trial.title: Free trial
nodo.plans.trial.text: {credits} credits to get to know it, once per account.
nodo.plans.monthly.title: Monthly plan
nodo.plans.monthly.text: Renews every month and credits do not roll over. You can cancel any time.
nodo.plans.topup.title: Top-up
nodo.plans.topup.text: For a busy month. Bought while the plan or the trial is active, and topped-up credits keep working after the month ends.
nodo.plans.price: The price is shown in your currency before you confirm: on the App Store on iPhone, iPad and Mac, and in Paddle’s secure checkout on Windows.
nodo.plans.account: You need to sign in to use Nodo. The rest of the app works without an account.
nodo.privacy.title: What Nodo sees and what it does not.
nodo.privacy.lead: It asks for your consent before the first message. Nodo is for people aged {age} or older.
nodo.privacy.sends.title: What is sent
nodo.privacy.sends.text: When you write to it, your message, the code and context of the screen you are viewing and a summary of your progress are sent. Nothing else.
nodo.privacy.provider.title: Who answers
nodo.privacy.provider.text: Answers are generated by an OpenAI model through the PseudoLearn server. Your device never talks to OpenAI directly and you need no key.
nodo.privacy.offline.title: Offline, no charge
nodo.privacy.offline.text: Without a connection Nodo does not answer and spends no credits. The rest of the app keeps working.
nodo.privacy.withdraw.title: You can withdraw it
nodo.privacy.withdraw.text: Withdraw your consent in Settings → Nodo at any time; it will ask again before the next message.
learn.seoDescription: {parts} parts, {lessons} lessons and {exercises} exercises to learn programming by solving problems, from the first program to objects, functions and tasks.
learn.hero.title: Learning to program is learning to solve problems.
learn.hero.lead: Written to be read in order, from the first question to the complete kiosk.
learn.route.title: {parts} parts, one staircase.
learn.route.lead: Each part opens with a question about how to think and most close with a project about the kiosk: {projects} in total. Open a part to see its lessons and the problem each one starts with.
learn.route.alt: The learning path in the app: the part 0 lessons with their problem, duration and solved required exercises.
learn.method.title: Five phases, always the same.
learn.method.lead: A lesson does not start with new syntax but with a problem. The PseudoLearn cycle takes you from the question to the tested program; at first it guides you through each phase, and over time you will do it without thinking.
learn.method.alt: A lesson in the app: the pizza problem, the block to try it before seeing the answer and the PseudoLearn cycle.
learn.method.caption: Each lesson says what you need beforehand, what you will learn and how long it takes.
learn.exercises.title: {kinds} ways to practice an idea.
learn.exercises.lead: Predicting the output, following an execution, finding the bug, breaking a program that looks right or designing the tests that catch it: each kind trains a different part of thinking like a programmer.
learn.exercises.requiredNote: {required} of the {exercises} exercises are required: the ones that complete each lesson. The rest is extra practice.
learn.progress.title: Your progress in plain sight. No grades.
learn.progress.lead: The My progress panel sums up what you have done and tells you what comes next. It gives no grades and does not punish attempts: an exercise is checked, tells you what is missing and you try again.
learn.progress.route.title: The path
learn.progress.route.text: A lesson is complete once you solve its required exercises; if it has none, opening it is enough.
learn.progress.exercises.title: The exercises
learn.progress.exercises.text: Solved by level and by kind, to see which skills you practice most.
learn.progress.concepts.title: The concepts
learn.progress.concepts.text: Which constructs you already used in your own algorithms: conditionals, loops, arrays, classes.
learn.progress.coverage.title: The specification
learn.progress.coverage.text: Which sections of the language your programs exercise and which are still missing.
learn.progress.next.title: The next step
learn.progress.next.text: The next lesson and how many required exercises remain in the current one.
learn.progress.promise: Your attempts never turn into a grade or a record that follows you around. Progress is stored on your device and, if you sign in, synced across yours.
route.kindText.predecir: You read a program and write exactly what it will print.
route.kindText.rastrear: You fill in the trace table step by step, as on paper.
route.kindText.ordenar: You put the lines of a shuffled program in order.
route.kindText.encontrar-error: A program that looks right fails in one case: you find it and fix it.
route.kindText.romperlo: You look for the input that makes a buggy program answer differently from the correct one.
route.kindText.disenar-pruebas: You write the cases that catch the buggy versions.
route.kindText.modificar: You change a working program so it does something new.
route.kindText.resolver: You write the whole program from the problem.
route.kindText.comparar: Two solutions that look the same: you decide how they differ.
route.kindText.clasificar: You place each value, idea or construct in its category.
route.kindText.explicar: You say in your own words what problem a program solves.
route.levelText.semilla: Just enough to fix the idea.
route.levelText.brote: The idea applied to a new case.
route.levelText.arbol: Combines the idea with what came before.
language.seoDescription: PseudoLearn is a complete programming language in Spanish or English: types, modules, objects, functions, concurrent tasks and a library, with a public, verified specification.
language.hero.title: A real programming language, in your language.
language.hero.lead: PseudoLearn is written in Spanish or English with the same rules. It has types, modules, objects, functions, concurrent tasks and a library for files, JSON and the internet. What you write is analyzed, run and can be watched step by step.
language.paradigms.title: One way of thinking per part.
language.paradigms.lead: Imperative, procedural, object-oriented, functional and concurrent, plus the outside world: files, JSON and the internet. Each part of the path starts with the question that gives rise to that way of thinking.
language.profiles.title: Two vocabularies, the same rules.
language.profiles.lead: Every keyword has an exact pair. The app translates a file’s vocabulary without changing its meaning, so you can start in your language and switch whenever you like.
language.environments.title: One .pseudo file, several places.
language.environments.lead: The same engine analyzes and runs your programs in the app, the editor and the terminal, so the result is the same everywhere.
language.env.app.title: The PseudoLearn app
language.env.app.text: For learning: editor, path, exercises and Nodo on macOS, Windows, iPhone and iPad.
language.env.app.f1: Errors as you type and step-by-step execution
language.env.app.f2: Flowchart, structogram, class diagram and trace table
language.env.app.f3: Tasks, arguments and equivalent code in Python and Rust

language.env.vscode.text: For bigger projects, in the editor you already use, also in VS Code for the Web.
language.env.vscode.f1: Highlighting, errors and help at the cursor
language.env.vscode.f2: Go to definition and rename across modules
language.env.vscode.f3: Running with input and debugging with breakpoints
language.env.cli.title: The terminal: pseudo
language.env.cli.text: For automation: check, run and compile programs from the command line.
language.env.cli.f3: Language server, debugger and MCP server for assistants
language.tools.title: Tools that explain instead of guessing.
language.tools.lead: Everything the app shows comes from the language engine: there is no second interpretation of your program.
language.tools.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics with context
language.tools.diagnostics.text: Each error marks its exact span and the related ones —the missing declaration, the extra closing— as you type.
language.tools.stepping.title: Observable execution
language.tools.stepping.text: Step by step at several speeds, with each object’s identity and each task’s timeline.
language.tools.diagrams.title: Diagrams drawn by the engine
language.tools.diagrams.text: Flowchart, structogram and class diagram generated from the program, not drawn separately.
language.tools.equivalent.title: Equivalent code
language.tools.equivalent.text: Your program projected to Python and Rust, line by line, to make the jump to an industry language.
language.tools.format.title: Formatting and translation
language.tools.format.text: One style for every program and the switch from Spanish to English in a single edit.
language.tools.agents.title: Ready for assistants
language.tools.agents.text: A language sheet for AI models and, in the terminal, an MCP server to check and run programs.

privacy.section.nodo.title: Nodo, the AI assistant
privacy.section.nodo.lead: Nodo is optional, requires signing in and asks for your consent before the first message. If you do not use it, nothing in this section applies to you.
privacy.section.nodo.sentText: When you write to Nodo, your message, the code and context of the screen you are viewing and a summary of your progress are sent. Your email and passwords are not sent.
privacy.section.nodo.providerText: Answers are generated by an OpenAI model, acting as a data processor through the PseudoLearn server. Your device does not connect to OpenAI directly, and OpenAI does not use these conversations to train its models.
privacy.section.nodo.keptText: PseudoLearn records the credit usage of each request —date and credits spent— to show your balance and bill correctly. It does not keep the content of conversations.
privacy.section.nodo.paymentsText: Subscriptions and top-ups are paid on the App Store (Apple) or with Paddle, acting as merchant of record. PseudoLearn receives the purchase confirmation, never your card details.
privacy.section.nodo.calloutText: Nodo is for people aged 13 or older. You can withdraw your consent in Settings → Nodo at any time; from then on nothing is sent until you accept again.
privacy.section.retention.itemNodo: Nodo credit records: while your account is active, to reconcile balances, renewals and purchase claims.
terms.section.pricing.text3: This website does not store bank details. The final price, in your currency and with applicable taxes, is shown before you confirm the purchase.
terms.section.nodo.title: Nodo, the AI assistant
terms.section.nodo.lead: Specific terms of the paid service.
terms.section.nodo.itemOptional: Nodo is optional and requires an account. No essential feature of the app depends on it.
terms.section.nodo.itemCredits: It runs on credits: the free trial includes 40 credits for 7 days, once per account; the monthly plan includes 300 credits that do not roll over between periods; top-ups of 150 credits are bought while the plan or trial is active and do not expire at the end of the month.
terms.section.nodo.itemRenewal: The subscription renews automatically every month unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the period.
terms.section.nodo.itemCancel: It is managed and cancelled from the App Store or from the Paddle portal, depending on where you bought it. Refunds follow that store’s policies.
terms.section.nodo.itemAccuracy: Nodo is an AI and can make mistakes. Check its answers; the code it suggests is verified with the engine, but that does not guarantee it solves your problem.
terms.section.nodo.itemAge: Nodo is for people aged 13 or older.
